dx_key: drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms
note: Rash, fever, hepatitis and kidney injury starting 20 days after a switch to nevirapine, with viral causes excluded, make the drug history decisive.
A post-vaccination prodrome followed by quadriparesis and bulbar palsy, with multifocal brainstem demyelination and CSF without oligoclonal bands, supports ADEM at one presentation.
Renal failure with haematuria, framed by NSAID use, smoking and recent pneumonia, is resolved by crescentic glomerulonephritis on biopsy and MPO-ANCA.
Recurrent cramping pain, vomiting and diarrhoea with negative travel, antibiotic and drug history frame a peripheral eosinophilia that multilevel biopsies confirm as eosinophilic gastroenteritis.

Fever, weight loss, facial palsy with taste loss, multifocal choroiditis and mediastinal adenopathy with infections excluded point to sarcoidosis; the TNF-inhibitor and travel history direct the workup.
Sex-worker contact three months earlier with a palmoplantar scaly rash, oral aphthae and generalised lymphadenopathy makes the sexual history the key to secondary syphilis.
Fasting neuroglycopenic episodes in a patient with metastatic carcinoma off metformin frame a workup where suppressed insulin, C-peptide and ketones with a high IGF-2:IGF-1 ratio decide.
A homeless man with myalgia, headache, conjunctival suffusion, jaundice, kidney failure and thrombocytopenia, with alternatives excluded, is a classic Weil disease presentation.
Two years of unilateral vision loss and low libido behind an acute meningitis point to an invasive pituitary tumour, which a prolactin of 9000 identifies.
A long, well-described thigh pain history frames a femoral cortical hyperostosis whose imaging, normal bone markers, negative genetics and benign biopsy lead to melorheostosis.

A strictly unilateral continuous headache with severe exacerbations and ipsilateral autonomic features is history-driven, though the facial gunshot injury adds secondary-cause noise and no indomethacin response is given.
Long-standing poorly controlled type 1 diabetes with microvascular complications frames painful thigh swelling whose MRI muscle oedema, with DVT excluded, fits diabetic myonecrosis.
New organising pneumonia on pre-existing fibrosis beginning after bucillamine was started, with infection and heart failure excluded, makes the medication timeline the key clue.
Progressive median-territory numbness and weakness without nocturnal symptoms frame an examination with thenar-triangle sensory loss and a proximal Tinel sign that localises to the forearm.
A heart-failure history without hypertension and with ACE-inhibitor intolerance frames a low-voltage ECG with echocardiographic hypertrophy, sparkling myocardium and restrictive filling.
Months of ascites and weight loss with exudative fluid, negative cytology, an unrevealing liver and cardiac workup and a strongly positive tuberculin test point to tuberculous peritonitis.
A four-year history of recurrent annular patches on sun-protected skin, only transiently steroid-responsive, frames a biopsy with epidermotropism and CD7 loss.
Back pain, weight loss and obstructive urinary symptoms with a hard nodular prostate, lytic bone lesions and PSA above 100 lead to metastatic prostate cancer.
Gradual vision loss on long-term brimonidine without contact lens or corneal history frames vascularised peripheral corneal opacities with a negative systemic workup.

An eight-month sequence of hearing loss, lung infiltrate, gingival hypertrophy, fevers and necrotic leg ulcers gives a rich history, confirmed by necrotising granulomatous vasculitis with infection excluded.
New cord and brain lesions three months after starting HAART with full adherence, a rising CD4 count and a suppressed viral load make the treatment timeline the key clue.
Sharp jaw and submandibular pain on the first bite of each meal, fading with later bites, with a normal exam and CT is a purely history-driven diagnosis.
An Afghan immigrant with months of indolent wrist pain failing treatment as sprain and osteoarthritis, a destructive carpal arthritis and a cold abscess makes skeletal tuberculosis the expert answer.
Sudden painful monocular vision loss in a young man with renal failure and malignant-range hypertension frames a normal fundus with optic nerve diffusion restriction.
Childhood sensorineural deafness, lifelong tetany and low birth weight in the history, with low-PTH hypocalcaemia, make HDR syndrome reachable.
Two months of postprandial pain relieved by vomiting with weight loss frame CT and MRI showing cystic duodenal wall thickening and groove soft tissue.
Focal seizures in seropositive rheumatoid arthritis with focal pachyleptomeningeal enhancement, very high anti-CCP and an extensive negative infection and malignancy workup.
Descending bulbar palsy with ptosis in a heroin skin-popper with deep abscesses is classic wound botulism; the clinician sentence naming botulism must be dropped.
Unilateral clear rhinorrhoea worse on straining after a childhood nasal injury and unresponsive to antiallergics is history-driven and confirmed by glucose-positive fluid.
Nocturnal fevers, arthralgia and cholestatic hepatitis with hepatosplenomegaly in a sheep farmer eating unpasteurised cheese is a history-driven diagnosis.
A worsening short-stepped gait out of proportion to a stable chemotherapy neuropathy frames ventriculomegaly without atrophy and a positive CSF tap test.
Years of self-injected intramuscular pentazocine explain the woody, calcified, contracted muscles at the injection sites, a history-driven diagnosis.
A month of fever, night sweats, weight loss and jaundice frames a fever of unknown origin, and splenomegaly, ferritin above 16,500, high triglycerides and low fibrinogen lead to HLH.
Sequential hemisensory episodes and later vertigo give dissemination in time from the history, confirmed by Dawson-finger lesions, cord lesions and CSF-specific oligoclonal bands.
A postpartum diabetic with unilateral panuveitis and yellow-white retinal infiltrates whose elicited history of persistent vaginal discharge (Candida on swab) is the key clue.
Fever beginning the night after filgrastim with new aortic wall inflammation on imaging and a negative infectious and autoimmune workup; the drug timeline from the history is the key clue.
Two months of headache and vomiting in a man born in Mexico with lymphocytic CSF containing eosinophils, obstructive hydrocephalus and an aqueductal cyst make neurocysticercosis reachable.
Night blindness from the 50s with later central loss and no family history frames the problem, and imaging of vertically oval atrophy beyond the arcades with reticular pseudodrusen decides.
Prolonged fever, weight loss, hepatosplenomegaly and pancytopenia with soil exposure from farm work in the Yangtze region and yeast forms in marrow; the exposure history matters.
Childhood xanthomas, Achilles thickening and a family history of xanthomas and sudden death with LDL 357 mg/dL make familial hypercholesterolemia clear from history and lipids.
Recurrent self-regressing facial swellings over years argue against a tumour, and high-amylase mucoid aspirate with a submandibular cystic lesion without a tail sign decides.
Polydipsia of 15 L a day with nocturia, amenorrhea and headache from the history, confirmed by water deprivation and a desmopressin response.
A detailed history of a slowly growing then rapidly enlarging axillary mass in an East African immigrant (hydatid differential) with a multiloculated cystic lesion on MRI.
Fever, graft tenderness and rising creatinine after stopping immunosuppression and starting checkpoint inhibitors; the medication history carries the diagnosis.

Months of headache, a seizure and progressive visual loss in an alert man with non-enhancing expansile T2 infiltration of several lobes after a negative HSV and toxin workup point to gliomatosis cerebri.
Accidental veterinary niclosamide ingestion followed by stable bilateral vision loss and bull's-eye maculopathy; the exposure history is decisive.

Chronic urticaria followed by fevers, bone pain and arthralgia with an IgM kappa paraprotein, neutrophilia and tibial uptake meets Schnitzler criteria; the prompt's tentative Still disease label is a distractor.
Three years of MTP pain with deformity, 2-hour morning stiffness and polyarthritis with erosions and ulnar deviation give seronegative rheumatoid arthritis behind the destructive hip.
Painless enlarging neck masses without B symptoms in a dialysis patient with generalized lymphadenopathy, eosinophilia and raised IgE make Kimura disease reachable.
Recurrent pneumonias since childhood in a non-smoker frame congenital bronchiectasis, and CT shows cystic bronchiectasis of 4th-6th order bronchi collapsing on expiration.
Ten days of syncope on sitting up with yawning and prodrome, reproduced in the ED as progressive sinus bradycardia, in a febrile COVID-19 patient with a structurally normal heart.
Watery diarrhea emerging during ten years of vismodegib with a negative infectious and celiac workup and apoptotic ileocolitis; the drug history is the key clue.

dx_key: stroke-like migraine attacks after radiation therapy
note: New migraine-like headache and homonymous hemianopia 25 years after cranial irradiation with no new enhancing lesion; the radiation history is decisive.
Headache and bitemporal field loss with anterior hypopituitarism and a symmetrically enlarged, homogeneously enhancing pituitary with a thick stalk point to lymphocytic hypophysitis.
A young woman with fever and tender necrotic cervical nodes unresponsive to several antibiotics and a negative infectious and autoimmune workup makes Kikuchi disease the leading answer.
Pruritic blisters with fever, weight loss and hair loss, tense bullae with malar and discoid rash, cytopenias, active urine sediment and positive ANA point to bullous SLE.
Daily fevers, salmon rash, arthritis, sore throat and splenomegaly with neutrophilic leukocytosis meet Yamaguchi criteria, with the tick bite as a history distractor.

dx_key: transient perivascular inflammation of the carotid artery
note: Focal pain and tenderness over the carotid bifurcation after a mild febrile prodrome with perivascular enhancing tissue and no stenosis or dissection gives TIPIC syndrome.
Bilateral iris transillumination, pigment dispersion, atonic pupils and high IOP without inflammation after topical moxifloxacin; the treatment history is a key clue.
Unprotected sex with multiple male partners, a palm-and-sole rash, cholestatic hepatitis and nephrotic proteinuria; the sexual history is the key clue to secondary syphilis.
Subacute symmetric leg weakness in a lung-transplant recipient on tacrolimus with albuminocytologic dissociation and demyelinating nerve conduction gives Guillain-Barre syndrome.
Six weeks of escalating cough with cough syncope, subconjunctival hemorrhages, facial swelling and marked lymphocytosis unresponsive to asthma and allergy treatment point to pertussis.
Fever, hematuria and acute kidney injury two weeks after starting sunitinib and then amoxicillin with a negative nephritic, TMA and infection workup point to drug-related interstitial nephritis.
A decade of acral enlargement, hyperhidrosis and scalp folds with clubbing, periostosis and normal labs make pachydermoperiostosis reachable from history and exam.
A smoker with squamous carcinoma in neck nodes, back pain, past heavy bleeding with missed gynecologic follow-up, a pelvic PET focus and hydronephrosis points to a cervical primary.
A pituitary mass with bitemporal hemianopia plus long-standing hypothyroid symptoms on review of systems and TSH above 100 make thyrotroph hyperplasia from primary hypothyroidism reachable.

Paresthesias, Raynaud phenomenon, weight loss and skin changes with demyelinating polyneuropathy, papilledema, thrombocytosis, adenopathy and sclerotic bone lesions lead to POEMS despite negative immunofixation.
Rapid orbital swelling, vision loss and ophthalmoplegia with pansinus disease in a patient on chronic prednisone with diabetic ketoacidosis make rhino-orbital mucormycosis reachable.
Two years of stereotyped 3-7 day flares of fever, rash, arthralgia, sore throat and diarrhea every 3 weeks with an extensive negative workup fit Yao syndrome.
Reliable account of jaundice and dark urine, drug exposures and a mother with autoimmune hemolytic anemia frames a hemolysis workup that the IgG-positive direct antiglobulin test decides.
Timeline of postprandial and fasting hypoglycemia, steroid response and bodybuilding supplements frames the workup; the supervised fast with very high insulin and anti-insulin antibodies decides.
Acute abdominal and back pain on warfarin for antiphospholipid syndrome with a supratherapeutic INR directs CT and a short synacthen test, which show bilateral adrenal lesions and adrenal failure.
Knee replacement with enoxaparin started 15 days earlier is the key history clue to thrombocytopenia with arterial and venous thromboses.
One week of dyspnea with fever and a history free of drugs, allergy and asthma frames heart failure that marked eosinophilia, troponin and echo decide.
Acquired adult-onset oral and nail pigmentation with no drugs, smoking or affected relatives is history that excludes key mimics; exam and a negative systemic workup decide.
Symptom onset two weeks after starting Sai-rei-to is the decisive history clue; the closing sentence attributing the illness to the herbal drug must be dropped.

Anorexia, weight loss and new skin tanning carry the diagnosis with profound hyponatremia and hyperkalemia; the closing sentence naming adrenal insufficiency must be dropped and cortisol results are not given.
Red painful photophobic eye after SMILE with new CPAP-related dryness frames the problem; slit-lamp limbitis with unstained peripheral infiltrates decides.
Long-term methotrexate with subacute dyspnea and no environmental exposures is the key history behind eosinophilia and upper-lobe opacities with a negative infection workup.
Focal throbbing pain over the carotid bifurcation without trauma or manipulation frames the problem; neck imaging excluding dissection and vasculitis decides.
Subacute dysarthria and ataxia after vaccination in an alert patient frame a cerebellar workup that MRI and lymphocytic CSF decide.
Right heart failure symptoms beginning weeks after cardiac surgery frame the problem; Kussmaul sign and constrictive physiology on echo decide.
Unexplained weight loss in a type 1 diabetic with denied thyroid symptoms directs thyroid testing; positive TPO antibodies with undetectable TSI and normal thyroglobulin decide.
A detailed account of neuropsychiatric and vestibular symptoms starting two weeks into mefloquine prophylaxis is the core of the diagnosis.
The steering-wheel chest blow before months of heart failure is the decisive history clue to the infarct pattern on ECG and cardiac MRI.
Neck mass with cough triggered by palpation and hoarseness frames a vagal lesion that the intensely enhancing carotid-sheath mass decides.
Hyperextension injury mechanism and catching frame the problem and MRI decides; the sentence interpreting the MRI as posterior impingement must be dropped.
Smoldering myeloma and earlier identical lesions that cleared on lenalidomide are history clues that, with the sclerosing biopsies, support a paraneoplastic process.
Starting brimonidine-brinzolamide drops three weeks earlier is the key history clue to bilateral angle closure with choroidal effusions.
History excluding diuretics, vomiting and diarrhea plus earlier weakness episodes frames hypokalemic alkalosis that urine studies and low urine calcium decide.
Thigh necrosis and bloody sputum with no drug or exposure history frame marked eosinophilia that a negative secondary-cause workup and marrow decide.
An antecedent cold and watery diarrhea three days before polyarthritis are the decisive history clues, with sterile joint fluid and negative serologies.
A detailed poor-diet, alcohol and tobacco history is the key clue to bilateral central scotomas with low folate.
Tongue pain with blue discoloration before ulceration and failed antimicrobials frame ischemic necrosis that inflammatory markers and beaded arteries on CT angiography decide.
Recent skull fracture, dizziness and no diuretic use frame hypovolemic hyponatremia that urine sodium, low uric acid and orthostatic testing decide.
Earlier gallstone cholangitis is the history clue behind Coombs-negative hemolysis with spherocytes and splenomegaly unmasked by E. coli pyelonephritis.
Second and third MCP arthropathy, new diabetes, low libido and skin pigmentation with cirrhosis form the classic picture, although iron studies are not given.
Insidious unilateral hand weakness in a young man that stopped progressing after three years is the history core of the diagnosis, supported by exam and EMG.
Eating raw shiitake 24 hours before flagellate dermatitis is the decisive history clue.
Abrupt adult-onset tics after stressors that the patient discloses on probing, with a normal neurological exam, make this a history-driven diagnosis.
